discussion.speaker: Fabienne KELLER
discussion.text:
Monsieur le Président – cher Roberts Zīle –, Madame la Vice-Présidente – chère Henna Virkkunen –, les récents blocages d’accès aux modèles d’intelligence artificielle les plus avancés ont été un signal d’alarme pour l’Europe. En quelques heures, nous avons découvert à quel point notre sécurité, nos administrations, nos entreprises dépendaient de technologies que nous ne contrôlons pas.

Le plan d’action européen sur la cybersécurité, qu’on est ravis de découvrir – mais je n’ai pas d’intelligence artificielle pour le lire, je n’ai pas encore tout pu lire –, doit donc intégrer une véritable stratégie de souveraineté. Cela signifie: investir dans des capacités européennes, soutenir des modèles de confiance, garantir un accès sécurisé aux technologies les plus avancées et renforcer nos infrastructures de calcul. Cela signifie qu’il est besoin de répondre à une question essentielle: comment l’Union peut-elle faire face au risque qu’un pays tiers puisse, du jour au lendemain, restreindre l’accès de l’Europe à des technologies d’IA essentielles?

Notre objectif n’est pas de nous isoler, mais de faire en sorte que la protection de nos citoyens, de leurs données, de leurs droits fondamentaux ne dépende jamais de décisions prises en dehors de l’Union.

translation.englishText:
Mr President – dear Roberts Zīle –, Madam Vice-President – dear Henna Virkkunen –, the recent blocking of access to the most advanced artificial intelligence models has been a wake-up call for Europe. In a few hours, we discovered the extent to which our security, our administrations, our businesses depended on technologies that we do not control.

The European cybersecurity action plan, which we are delighted to discover – but I do not have artificial intelligence to read it, I have not yet been able to read everything –, must therefore integrate a genuine sovereignty strategy. This means: investing in European capabilities, supporting trusted models, guaranteeing secure access to the most advanced technologies, and strengthening our computing infrastructure. This means there is a need to answer an essential question: how can the Union face the risk that a third country could, overnight, restrict Europe's access to essential AI technologies?

Our goal is not to isolate ourselves, but to ensure that the protection of our citizens, their data, and their fundamental rights never depends on decisions made outside the Union.
translation.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président – cher Roberts Zīle –, Madame la Vice-Présidente – chère Henna Virkkunen –, les récents blocages d’accès aux modèles d’intelligence artificielle les plus avancés ont été un signal d’alarme pour l’Europe. En quelques heures, nous avons découvert à quel point notre sécurité, nos administrations, nos entreprises dépendaient de technologies que nous ne contrôlons pas.

Le plan d’action européen sur la cybersécurité, qu’on est ravis de découvrir – mais je n’ai pas d’intelligence artificielle pour le lire, je n’ai pas encore tout pu lire –, doit donc intégrer une véritable stratégie de souveraineté. Cela signifie: investir dans des capacités européennes, soutenir des modèles de confiance, garantir un accès sécurisé aux technologies les plus avancées et renforcer nos infrastructures de calcul. Cela signifie qu’il est besoin de répondre à une question essentielle: comment l’Union peut-elle faire face au risque qu’un pays tiers puisse, du jour au lendemain, restreindre l’accès de l’Europe à des technologies d’IA essentielles?

Notre objectif n’est pas de nous isoler, mais de faire en sorte que la protection de nos citoyens, de leurs données, de leurs droits fondamentaux ne dépende jamais de décisions prises en dehors de l’Union.

discussion.speaker: Sven SIMON
discussion.text:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, meine sehr geehrten Damen und Herren! Wir reden heute über künstliche Intelligenz, aber in Wahrheit reden wir über Europas Zukunft, und diese Zukunft entsteht gerade woanders. Europa verfügt über lediglich rund 5 % der weltweiten KI‑Rechenkapazität; die Vereinigten Staaten von Amerika liegen bei fast 75 %. Amerikanische Digitalkonzerne investieren hunderte Milliarden in Rechenzentren, Chips, Netze und Energie. Was macht Europa? Wir prüfen, regulieren, wir verzögern.

KI braucht nicht nur gute Absichten; KI braucht Strom, Flächen, Glasfaser, Genehmigungen und Tempo, aber genau dort scheitern wir. Und wir haben auch in der Debatte schon gehört, dass das teilweise gewollt ist von den politischen Mitbewerbern. Die KI‑Verordnung, denke ich, steht für diese europäische Krankheit: Erst kommen die Auflagen, dann vielleicht irgendwann die Wertschöpfung.

So wird Europa nicht souverän werden. Wir brauchen disruptive Entscheidungen, den konsequenten Abbau jener Partikularinteressen, die wir über Jahre in Gesetze gegossen haben und die heute fast jede Zukunftsinvestition blockieren.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! Today we are talking about artificial intelligence, but in truth we are talking about Europe's future, and this future is currently being created elsewhere. Europe has only around 5% of global AI computing capacity; the United States of America is at almost 75%. American tech corporations are investing hundreds of billions in data centers, chips, networks, and energy. What is Europe doing? We are vetting, we are regulating, we are delaying.

AI needs more than good intentions; AI needs electricity, land, fiber optics, permits, and speed, and that is precisely where we are failing. And we have also heard in the debate that this is partly intended by political competitors. The AI Act, I think, stands for this European disease: first come the regulations, then perhaps value creation at some point.

This is not how Europe will become sovereign. We need disruptive decisions, the consistent dismantling of those vested interests that we have poured into laws over years and that today block almost every investment in the future.

discussion.speaker: Brando BENIFEI
discussion.text:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il "kill switch" non è più un'ipotesi: è stato premuto. A giugno, con una firma, Donald Trump ha chiuso l'accesso al modello di intelligenza artificiale più potente al mondo, anche all'Agenzia per la cibersicurezza europea, che l'aveva appena ottenuto.

Le nostre regole decidono come possiamo usare l'intelligenza artificiale in sicurezza, oggi, altri decidono se possiamo usarla: questa è la dipendenza.

Quindi, bene il piano sulla cybersecurity, ma senza fondi e scadenze vincolanti rischia di restare un elenco di intenzioni. Servono risorse per l'Ufficio europeo per l'intelligenza artificiale, che avrà sempre più responsabilità, una legge su cloud e AI davvero ambiziosa, e capacità pubblica europea e non sussidi ai giganti da cui già dipendiamo.

E nessuno si azzardi a pensare di comprare l'accesso ai modelli americani, allentando in segreto l'applicazione delle nostre leggi. La sicurezza digitale europea non va più affittata a nessuno, va costruita, con apertura, ma con determinazione, per difendere i nostri interessi.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, the "kill switch" is no longer a hypothesis: it has been pressed. In June, with a single signature, Donald Trump cut off access to the world's most powerful artificial intelligence model, even for the European Cybersecurity Agency, which had just obtained it.

Our rules decide how we can use artificial intelligence safely; today, others decide whether we can use it: this is dependence.

Therefore, the cybersecurity plan is good, but without funds and binding deadlines, it risks remaining a list of intentions. Resources are needed for the European Artificial Intelligence Office, which will have increasing responsibilities, a truly ambitious cloud and AI law, and European public capacity, not subsidies to the giants we already depend on.

And let no one dare think of buying access to American models by secretly easing the enforcement of our laws. European digital security must no longer be rented out to anyone; it must be built, with openness, but with determination, to defend our interests.

discussion.speaker: Engin EROGLU
discussion.text:
Herr Präsident! Sehr geehrte Frau Kommissarin, ich danke Ihnen ausdrücklich für Ihren Bericht zur Sicherheit im Cyberraum und zu künstlicher Intelligenz, weil die Sicherheit im Cyberraum sich massiv verändert durch den Einsatz von künstlicher Intelligenz. Und selbstverständlich haben die Sicherheitsbehörden dort ihre Aufgabe, so wie auch im öffentlichen Raum, und natürlich muss die Politik den Rahmen gestalten, damit Sicherheitsbehörden arbeiten können.

Zu dem, was Sie aber nicht gesagt haben, Frau Kommissarin: Sie haben nichts zu Quantencomputern gesagt. Was ist die Strategie der Europäischen Union bei Quantencomputern? Wie schützen wir unsere Infrastruktur in Quantencomputer-Technologie, die auf uns zukommt?

Sie haben auch nichts dazu gesagt, dass ja neben den vielen Kriminellen, die unternehmerisch tätig sind, um andere Unternehmer zu betrügen, auch Drittstaaten ganz konkret Hacker dafür einsetzen, um die Europäische Union und ihre Mitgliedstaaten anzugreifen, ganz konkret die Bundesregierung Deutschland: Die Regierungsbehörden werden täglich mit 800 Hackerangriffen angegriffen. Da dürfen wir nicht nur reparieren, sondern müssen auch agieren; wir müssen Hackerangriffe von Drittstaaten zurück angreifen. Und da ist meine Frage: Was tun Sie dort? Haben Sie Gespräche mit Herrn Kubilius geführt?

translation.englishText:
Mr President! Dear Commissioner, I explicitly thank you for your report on cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, because cybersecurity is changing massively through the use of artificial intelligence. And of course, the security authorities have their task there, just as in the public space, and of course politics must shape the framework so that security authorities can work.

Regarding what you did not say, however, Commissioner: You said nothing about quantum computers. What is the European Union's strategy on quantum computers? How do we protect our infrastructure in quantum computer technology that is coming towards us?

You also said nothing about the fact that, alongside the many criminals who operate as entrepreneurs to defraud other entrepreneurs, third countries also specifically deploy hackers to attack the European Union and its member states, specifically the Federal Government of Germany: Government authorities are attacked daily with 800 cyberattacks. There, we must not only repair, but also act; we must counter-attack cyberattacks from third countries. And my question is: What are you doing there? Have you held discussions with Mr Kubilius?

discussion.speaker: Nicola ZINGARETTI
discussion.text:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, l'action plan che la Commissione ha appena presentato rappresenta un passaggio non risolutivo, ma certo importante nel percorso verso la sovranità tecnologica europea.

Autonomia non è autarchia, certo, ma è protagonismo, perché l'Unione non può continuare a dipendere da processi opachi e decisioni unilaterali di paesi terzi.

E i recenti episodi legati proprio alle restrizioni sull'accesso a modelli di frontiera dimostrano quanto questa vulnerabilità sia oggi una questione di sicurezza, ancora prima che di competitività.

L'Europa, quindi, deve costruire una propria capacità tecnologica autonoma nell'intelligenza artificiale di frontiera e questo richiede una scelta politica chiara.

Oltre ai provvedimenti, però, che si stanno finalmente adottando, servono investimenti adeguati, pubblici e privati, capaci di colmare il divario con Stati Uniti e Cina.

Per questo, la scelta dei governi su un bilancio previsionale per l'Europa, che hanno fatto è un errore: è timido, è sbagliato e in parte in contraddizione con le scelte giuste che stiamo facendo.

Senza risorse concrete, non si va da nessuna parte.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, the action plan that the Commission has just presented represents a non-definitive, but certainly important step on the path towards European technological sovereignty.

Autonomy is not autarky, of course, but it is leadership, because the Union cannot continue to depend on opaque processes and unilateral decisions by third countries.

And recent episodes linked precisely to restrictions on access to frontier models demonstrate how this vulnerability is today a security issue, even before being a competitiveness issue.

Europe, therefore, must build its own autonomous technological capacity in frontier artificial intelligence, and this requires a clear political choice.

Beyond the measures, however, that are finally being adopted, adequate investments, both public and private, are needed, capable of bridging the gap with the United States and China.

For this reason, the choice that governments made regarding a forward-looking budget for Europe is a mistake: it is timid, it is wrong, and in part in contradiction with the right choices we are making.

Without concrete resources, you do not get anywhere.

discussion.speaker: Sophia KIRCHER
discussion.text:
Herr Präsident, geschätzte Frau Exekutiv-Vizepräsidentin der Kommission, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! KI und Quantencomputing entscheiden darüber, ob wir wirtschaftlich erfolgreich sind. Cybersicherheit entscheidet darüber, ob wir in Zukunft überhaupt noch handlungsfähig sind. Deshalb müssen wir dringend die Weichen für die Zukunft stellen.

Es ist positiv, dass die Kommission nun diesen Aktionsplan vorgestellt hat, allerdings geht es jetzt um die Umsetzung. Und eines ist klar: Unsere KMU brauchen mehr digitale Sicherheit, schnelle Hilfe im Ernstfall und vor allem keine neuen Bürokratielasten. Europa muss digital, souverän und wettbewerbsfähig werden – mit europäischen Cloudlösungen, einer eigenen digitalen Infrastruktur und Exzellenz beim Quantencomputing. Denn wer die Schlüsseltechnologien entwickelt, sichert Wohlstand, Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Arbeitsplätze und setzt auch die Spielregeln für unsere Zukunft.

Und Cyberkompetenzen müssen auch in unsere Klassenzimmer. Sie müssen dort so selbstverständlich unterrichtet werden wie Lesen, Rechnen und Schreiben, denn die wichtigste Firewall sitzt vor den Bildschirmen.

Die Botschaft ist klar: Digitale Souveränität und Sicherheit sind keine technische Frage; sie sind die Grundlage unserer Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, unserer Sicherheit und unserer Freiheit.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, esteemed Executive Vice-President of the Commission, dear colleagues! AI and quantum computing will determine whether we are economically successful. Cybersecurity will determine whether we will still be able to act at all in the future. Therefore, we urgently need to set the course for the future.

It is positive that the Commission has now presented this action plan, but now it is all about implementation. And one thing is clear: our SMEs need more digital security, rapid assistance in emergencies and, above all, no new bureaucratic burdens. Europe must become digital, sovereign and competitive – with European cloud solutions, its own digital infrastructure and excellence in quantum computing. Because whoever develops the key technologies secures prosperity, competitiveness, jobs and also sets the rules of the game for our future.

And cyber skills must also find their way into our classrooms. They must be taught there as naturally as reading, writing and arithmetic, because the most important firewall sits in front of the screens.

The message is clear: digital sovereignty and security are not a technical question; they are the basis of our competitiveness, our security and our freedom.

discussion.speaker: Maria GUZENINA
discussion.text:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, in Europe, in cybersecurity, our biggest vulnerability is believing that we are protected and that we have time, which we are not and which we do not have.

As the rapporteur for IMCO on the Cybersecurity Act 2, I welcome the action plan Commissioner Virkkunen has presented today. European society needs to be defended from all angles. Our cyber ecosystem needs to be protected urgently, but my worry is that the funding is not adequate.

Experts speak already of 'Q-Day': the day quantum computing becomes powerful enough to break the encryption that protects our banking system, critical infrastructure, weapon systems, communications and data. Hostile actors are already collecting our encrypted data, hoping to decrypt it as soon as possible.

So cybersecurity is not a matter just of national security. It's about economic resilience and, finally, democracy...

(The President cut off the speaker)

discussion.speaker: Sofie ERIKSSON
discussion.text:
Mr President, things are going so fast. A lot of people feel like we are losing control, and billionaire oligarchs act like there is no choice. But to me, they sound like: 'We are the Borg. You will be assimilated. Resistance is futile.'

This endless race: catch up, keep up, don't fall behind. But the only question worth asking cannot be how fast we can plug ourselves into someone else's system. Our hospitals, our power grids, our most sensitive government data are dependent on systems we do not own and do not control.

The line must be drawn here. We welcome the action plan. We need our own public, accountable, democratically controlled capability, even if it's harder – because, unlike the humanoids assimilated by the Borg, we still get to choose our way forward: with technology, with democracy, with humanity.

discussion.speaker: José CEPEDA
discussion.text:
Señor presidente, señora Virkkunen, comparto este plan y, fundamentalmente, sus tres objetivos, que hablan de promover, fomentar y animar, pero, mientras en ese plan se utilizan estos verbos, la realidad es que la amenaza se está ya ejecutando en tiempo real.

Por lo tanto, me gustaría decirle que creo que es muy importante implementar la Directiva SRI 2 en el conjunto del sistema europeo. Hay que exigir, financiar y también sancionar, por qué no decirlo.

ENISA, que es el gran pilar en el que usted se basa, tiene un gran déficit y es que plantea 341 millones en siete años y, lamentablemente, en la práctica en un año o año y medio la computación cuántica va a estar aquí y eso va a ser una gran amenaza.

Fíjense, yo creo que aparte de hablar de infraestructuras críticas, también tenemos que hablar de personas. Por ejemplo, el ejemplo que dio ayer el Gobierno de España —con mi querido amigo Óscar López— al implementar una gran coalición con Francia y Kenia, junto con las Naciones Unidas, va en esa dirección, para precisamente proteger también de la IA a nuestros menores, que es un reto muy importante para el futuro.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Mrs Virkkunen, I share this plan and, fundamentally, its three objectives, which speak of promoting, encouraging and fostering, but while these verbs are used in that plan, the reality is that the threat is already being carried out in real time.

Therefore, I would like to tell you that I believe it is very important to implement the NIS 2 Directive across the entire European system. We must demand, finance and also penalize, why not say so.

ENISA, which is the great pillar on which you base yourself, has a major deficit and that is that it proposes 341 million over seven years and, unfortunately, in practice in a year or a year and a half quantum computing is going to be here and that is going to be a major threat.

Look, I believe that apart from talking about critical infrastructure, we also have to talk about people. For example, the example given yesterday by the Government of Spain —with my dear friend Óscar López— by implementing a major coalition with France and Kenya, together with the United Nations, goes in that direction, precisely to also protect our minors from AI, which is a very important challenge for the future.

discussion.speaker: Salvatore DE MEO
discussion.text:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, il piano d'azione europeo sulla cibersicurezza e l'intelligenza artificiale rappresenta una scelta strategica per rafforzare la sicurezza, la competitività e la resilienza dell'Unione.

Perché proteggere reti, infrastrutture critiche e i nostri dati significa tutelare le nostre imprese e garantire la continuità dei servizi essenziali ai cittadini.

L'intelligenza artificiale è una leva decisiva per l'innovazione, per l'autonomia strategica e per la nostra sicurezza. Allo stesso tempo, se utilizzata da attori ostili, può trasformarsi in uno strumento capace di colpire i nostri sistemi, le nostre economie e persino le nostre democrazie.

Per questo, l'Europa deve governare questo processo e non aspettarne l'evoluzione. Come autorevolmente richiamato dalla lettera enciclica "Magnifica Humanitas" di Papa Leone XIV, il progresso tecnologico acquista il suo pieno valore solo quando è al servizio della persona umana e ne custodisce la dignità.

Per questo, l'intelligenza artificiale deve restare uno strumento nelle mani dell'uomo e mai un sostituto del suo giudizio e della sua responsabilità. Solo così l'Europa saprà vincere le sfide della cibersicurezza, costruendo un futuro più forte, protetto e profondamente libero.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, the European action plan on cybersecurity and artificial intelligence represents a strategic choice to strengthen the Union's security, competitiveness and resilience.

Because protecting networks, critical infrastructure and our data means safeguarding our businesses and ensuring the continuity of essential services to citizens.

Artificial intelligence is a decisive lever for innovation, strategic autonomy and our security. At the same time, if used by hostile actors, it can turn into a tool capable of striking our systems, our economies and even our democracies.

For this reason, Europe must govern this process and not wait for its evolution. As authoritatively recalled by the encyclical letter "Magnifica Humanitas" by Pope Leo XIV, technological progress acquires its full value only when it is at the service of the human person and preserves their dignity.

For this reason, artificial intelligence must remain a tool in human hands and never a substitute for human judgment and responsibility. Only in this way will Europe be able to win the challenges of cybersecurity, building a stronger, protected and deeply free future.
translation.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, il piano d'azione europeo sulla cibersicurezza e l'intelligenza artificiale rappresenta una scelta strategica per rafforzare la sicurezza, la competitività e la resilienza dell'Unione.

Perché proteggere reti, infrastrutture critiche e i nostri dati significa tutelare le nostre imprese e garantire la continuità dei servizi essenziali ai cittadini.

L'intelligenza artificiale è una leva decisiva per l'innovazione, per l'autonomia strategica e per la nostra sicurezza. Allo stesso tempo, se utilizzata da attori ostili, può trasformarsi in uno strumento capace di colpire i nostri sistemi, le nostre economie e persino le nostre democrazie.

Per questo, l'Europa deve governare questo processo e non aspettarne l'evoluzione. Come autorevolmente richiamato dalla lettera enciclica "Magnifica Humanitas" di Papa Leone XIV, il progresso tecnologico acquista il suo pieno valore solo quando è al servizio della persona umana e ne custodisce la dignità.

Per questo, l'intelligenza artificiale deve restare uno strumento nelle mani dell'uomo e mai un sostituto del suo giudizio e della sua responsabilità. Solo così l'Europa saprà vincere le sfide della cibersicurezza, costruendo un futuro più forte, protetto e profondamente libero.

discussion.speaker: Henna Virkkunen
discussion.text:
Mr President, honourable Members, thank you for your interventions and very valuable comments. I think it is important to underline that, really, this action plan is not the end of our discussion, because this is now the real beginning of European efforts to ensure that AI becomes a strategic asset for our security, not a systematic vulnerability. And this is the European way for AI and cybersecurity: built on trust, transparency and safety. These are the conditions for ensuring that the most advanced AI models can be deployed in Europe safely, used for cybersecurity responsibly, and also turned into instruments of our security rather than weapons against our societies.

Many of you were underlining very much the importance of tech sovereignty and its crucial pillar in our action plan, really to scale and boost our own capabilities in this area. But, as you said, also, and I underlined, massive investments are really needed now and urgently in this area.

Also, the second priority in our action plan and an important pillar is, of course, to prepare our cybersecurity environment and also be able to fix the vulnerabilities fast. Here we will work very closely with our industries and Member States.

The third pillar is about evaluating, testing and having access to these capable models, and there we are also working with the blueprint. So we will need to move quickly. It is important to underline that now we have nine key actions identified here and seven of them we will implement now already during the autumn. We will work very closely with our Member States, with this House, with our industry, with the open‑source community, and with our international partners, of course, because this is a challenge that Europe cannot afford to face alone or too late.

discussion.speaker: Sunčana GLAVAK
discussion.text:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, digitalna suverenost nije pitanje protekcionizma, nego otpornosti. Cilj nije zamijeniti jednu ovisnost drugom, već smanjenje strateške ovisnosti i povećanje europske konkurentnosti.

Stoga pozdravljam akcijski plan Komisije jer umjetna inteligencija više nije samo pokretač inovacija, već i novi čimbenik europske sigurnosti. Danas već više od 80 posto phishing kampanja koristi elemente generativne umjetne inteligencije, a kibernetičke prijetnje razvijaju se, nažalost, brže od naših obrambenih sustava.

Pred nama su ključna pitanja, hoćemo li dovoljno ulagati, imamo li stručnjake za koordinaciju i za zaštitu kritične infrastrukture i jesmo li spremni na prijelaz za post-kvantnu kriptografiju prije nego što kvantna računala ugroze današnje sustave enkripcije i činimo li na kraju dovoljno da bismo zaštitili djecu i naše osobne podatke.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, digital sovereignty is not a question of protectionism, but of resilience. The goal is not to replace one dependency with another, but to reduce strategic dependency and increase European competitiveness.

Therefore, I welcome the Commission's action plan because artificial intelligence is no longer just a driver of innovation, but also a new factor in European security. Today, more than 80 percent of phishing campaigns already use elements of generative artificial intelligence, and cyber threats are developing, unfortunately, faster than our defense systems.

Key questions lie ahead of us: will we invest enough, do we have the experts for coordination and for the protection of critical infrastructure, and are we ready for the transition to post-quantum cryptography before quantum computers threaten today's encryption systems, and are we finally doing enough to protect children and our personal data.

discussion.speaker: Juan Fernando LÓPEZ AGUILAR
discussion.text:
Señor presidente, OpenAI, Mythos, Anthropos, inteligencia artificial de frontera... ¿Por qué se revuelven contra el poder regulatorio de la Unión Europea? Porque lo temen.

Por tanto, una estrategia de ciberseguridad en inteligencia artificial que sea netamente europea tiene que abundar en lo que la distingue y exactamente en lo que los mastodontes temen: su transparencia, su dotación de cuentas, su sujeción a derechos fundamentales. Y se debe explicar, además, que no lo hacemos por pánico a una revolución tecnológica imparable, sino porque nos importa la supervisión humana, que es la que las hace consistentes con nuestro estándar de derechos fundamentales.

Estamos dispuestos —claro que sí— a reconvertir nuestro mercado de trabajo sabiendo que la inteligencia artificial tendrá un impacto tremendo sobre muchos empleos que ahora existen y no existirán pasado mañana. Pero a lo que no estamos dispuestos es a que un algoritmo imponga un veredicto de culpabilidad en la justicia. Eso es lo que diferencia al modelo europeo y lo que tiene que preservar la ciberseguridad en inteligencia artificial distintivamente europea.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, OpenAI, Mythos, Anthropos, frontier artificial intelligence... Why are they rebelling against the regulatory power of the European Union? Because they fear it.

Therefore, a cybersecurity strategy in artificial intelligence that is purely European must focus on what distinguishes it and precisely on what the mastodons fear: its transparency, its accountability, its subjection to fundamental rights. And it must also be explained that we do not do this out of panic of an unstoppable technological revolution, but because we care about human supervision, which is what makes them consistent with our standard of fundamental rights.

We are willing—of course we are—to reconvert our labor market knowing that artificial intelligence will have a tremendous impact on many jobs that now exist and will not exist the day after tomorrow. But what we are not willing to do is to have an algorithm impose a guilty verdict in justice. That is what differentiates the European model and what distinctively European artificial intelligence cybersecurity must preserve.

discussion.speaker: Sebastian TYNKKYNEN
discussion.text:
Arvoisa puhemies, tuon esille muutamia tilastoja tekoälystä. Suomessa tekoälyä käyttävien yritysten osuus on noussut melkein 38 prosenttiin. Se on EU:n keskiarvoon verrattuna lähes kaksi kertaa enemmän.

Mutta mikä Euroopan tekoälykehitystä oikein kurjistaa? Luvut tarjoavat vastauksen. EU:n tasolla isoista yrityksistä tekoälyn käyttöprosentti yltää jopa 55 prosenttiin. Sitten tulee mutta: EU:n tasolla vain 30 prosenttia keskisuurista ja vain 17 prosenttia pienistä yrityksistä käyttää tekoälyä.

EU:n tekoälysääntelyn noudattamiseen tarvitaan suuria resursseja, joita pienemmillä yrityksillä ei yksinkertaisesti ole. Euroopan rooli tulevaisuuden kansainvälisellä näyttämöllä on kiinni siitä, kuinka hyödynnämme uusinta teknologiaa. Tämä rooli lähtee rakentumaan, kun lakkaamme olemasta sääntelyn suurvalta.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, I will present a few statistics on artificial intelligence. In Finland, the proportion of companies using artificial intelligence has risen to almost 38 percent. Compared to the EU average, that is almost twice as much.

But what is actually stifling Europe's artificial intelligence development? The figures provide the answer. At the EU level, the usage percentage of large companies reaches up to 55 percent. Then comes the catch: at the EU level, only 30 percent of medium-sized and only 17 percent of small companies use artificial intelligence.

Complying with EU artificial intelligence regulations requires large resources that smaller companies simply do not have. Europe's role on the future international stage depends on how well we utilize the latest technology. This role begins to take shape when we stop being a superpower of regulation.

discussion.speaker: Lukas SIEPER
discussion.text:
Mr President,

(Speaking into a smartphone)

Hey Mistral, what do you think about the action plan on cybersecurity and AI?

One second please.

(Reading from the smartphone)

'The European Commission's action plan on cybersecurity and AI, unveiled today, tackles AI's dual role, both as a cyberthreat and a defence tool. By Q4 2026, it will deliver a European blueprint for structured access to advanced AI models and a secure testing platform with ENISA, practical guidelines for AI-based threat protection and the EU Grand Challenge for home-grown solutions. Strengths: proactive, holistic, collaborative. Risks: uncertain access to US frontier models, ENISA's capacity to execute. With the AI Act's cybersecurity rules starting on 2 August, this plan is Europe's practical playbook. Verdict: the necessary execution speed will decide if Europe can lead on safe AI cybersecurity.'

Well, now, of course, everything in that is true except for the fact that this was pre-prepared, because European AI is way too slow to deliver this result within 10 seconds.

discussion.speaker: Ondřej DOSTÁL
discussion.text:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, in the ASEAN Delegation of the European Parliament, we discussed the issue of cyber scamming in Myanmar. There are non-state actors, mafias, who run basically slave factories on cyber scams, targeting people all around the world, including in Europe.

So I spoke to diplomats from the region and received very positive replies from China, Cambodia and Myanmar itself, which now has a stable government, and they are genuinely willing to work on this issue with us. But the Commission told us we will not cooperate, we will not even speak to Myanmar because they are not a democratically elected government.

So I ask you, is it better to do virtue signalling and let a grand mass in Europe get scammed? Or is it better to work together on resolving this important problem?

discussion.speaker: Michał SZCZERBA

Szanowny Panie Przewodniczący! AI, sztuczna inteligencja, jest z jednej strony narzędziem wzmacniającym cyberbezpieczeństwo, ale to również źródło nowych wyzwań. To, co jest ważne, to przede wszystkim współpraca, wymiana informacji, wspólne mechanizmy reagowania i koordynacja działań. Panie Przewodniczący Zīle, możemy dzisiaj wspólnie powiedzieć: nasze zadanie zostało wykonane. Mamy stanowisko Parlamentu Europejskiego w sprawie ważnego rozporządzenia, jakim jest mobilność wojskowa, i w przyszłym tygodniu rozpoczniemy wspólnie negocjacje międzyinstytucjonalne.

Ale to, z czego się szczególnie cieszę i czym chciałbym się przed Wysoką Izbą pochwalić, to przede wszystkim to, że uwzględniliśmy problematykę bezpieczeństwa systemów z problematyką bezpieczeństwa łączności w naszej regulacji. To jest bardzo ważna podstawa do wspólnych, dalszych działań.

translation.englishText:
Mr. President! AI, artificial intelligence, is on the one hand a tool strengthening cybersecurity, but it is also a source of new challenges. What is important is, above all, cooperation, exchange of information, joint response mechanisms and coordination of actions. Mr. President Zīle, we can say together today: our task has been accomplished. We have the position of the European Parliament on an important regulation, which is military mobility, and next week we will jointly start interinstitutional negotiations.

But what I am particularly pleased with and what I would like to boast about before this High House is, above all, the fact that we included the issue of systems security along with communications security issues in our regulation. This is a very important basis for joint, further actions.

discussion.speaker: Laura BALLARÍN CEREZA
discussion.text: Los socialistas hemos subrayado que Europa debe reforzar su soberanía tecnológica en inteligencia artificial y ciberseguridad. La seguridad del siglo XXI depende también del control de datos, algoritmos y tecnologías digitales, por lo que Europa no puede depender de capacidades desarrolladas fuera de sus fronteras. Aunque se valora el plan de acción sobre ciberseguridad e inteligencia artificial de la Comisión Europea, desde el Grupo S&D hemos señalado que la regulación no es suficiente: es necesario aumentar la inversión pública, apoyar a las empresas europeas y aplicar medidas efectivas para garantizar la seguridad, lo que incluye el cumplimiento de normativas como la Directiva SRI 2. También hemos alertado sobre nuevas amenazas, como la computación cuántica, y subrayado la importancia de proteger no solo las infraestructuras críticas, sino también a los ciudadanos —especialmente a los menores— frente a los riesgos de la inteligencia artificial.

translation.englishText: We socialists have stressed that Europe must strengthen its technological sovereignty in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. Twenty-first-century security also depends on the control of data, algorithms, and digital technologies, which is why Europe cannot depend on capabilities developed outside its borders. Although the European Commission's action plan on cybersecurity and artificial intelligence is valued, the S&D Group has pointed out that regulation is not enough: it is necessary to increase public investment, support European companies, and apply effective measures to guarantee security, which includes compliance with regulations such as the NIS 2 Directive. We have also warned about new threats, such as quantum computing, and stressed the importance of protecting not only critical infrastructure, but also citizens—especially minors—from the risks of artificial intelligence.

discussion.speaker: Vasile DÎNCU
discussion.text:
Securitatea cibernetică și inteligența artificială se influențează reciproc și trebuie gândite ca parte a aceleiași strategii europene de securitate. Planul de acțiune poate fi consolidat prin câteva măsuri foarte concrete.

Toate sistemele de inteligență artificială utilizate în administrația publică și în infrastructurile critice ar trebui să fie supuse unor audituri independente înainte de implementare și unor evaluări periodice după punerea în funcțiune.

Europa are nevoie de un mecanism comun de alertă și schimb rapid de informații privind incidentele cibernetice și vulnerabilitățile IA, deoarece timpul este adesea mai important decât resursele.

O altă prioritate este investiția în oameni. Deficitul de specialiști în securitate cibernetică devine o vulnerabilitate strategică. Avem nevoie de programe europene de formare, de exerciții comune și de o mai bună circulație a expertizei între statele membre.

Nu putem ignora nici impactul asupra democrației. IA face posibilă producerea la scară industrială a conținutului manipulator, a atacurilor informaționale și a campaniilor de dezinformare. Reziliența democratică trebuie să facă parte din politica europeană de securitate cibernetică.

Autonomia tehnologică nu este un slogan. Dacă infrastructura digitală a Europei depinde de tehnologii pe care nu le controlăm, vulnerabilitatea noastră rămâne structurală. Acesta este motivul pentru care investiția în capacități europene trebuie să devină o prioritate strategică.

translation.englishText:
Cybersecurity and artificial intelligence influence each other and must be conceived as part of the same European security strategy. The action plan can be strengthened through a few very concrete measures.

All artificial intelligence systems used in public administration and critical infrastructure should be subject to independent audits before deployment and periodic evaluations after commissioning.

Europe needs a common alert and rapid information exchange mechanism regarding cyber incidents and AI vulnerabilities, because time is often more important than resources.

Another priority is investment in people. The shortage of cybersecurity specialists is becoming a strategic vulnerability. We need European training programs, joint exercises, and better circulation of expertise between member states.

We cannot ignore the impact on democracy either. AI makes possible the industrial-scale production of manipulative content, informational attacks, and disinformation campaigns. Democratic resilience must be part of European cybersecurity policy.

Technological autonomy is not a slogan. If Europe's digital infrastructure depends on technologies we do not control, our vulnerability remains structural. This is why investment in European capabilities must become a strategic priority.
translation.sourceText:
Securitatea cibernetică și inteligența artificială se influențează reciproc și trebuie gândite ca parte a aceleiași strategii europene de securitate. Planul de acțiune poate fi consolidat prin câteva măsuri foarte concrete.

Toate sistemele de inteligență artificială utilizate în administrația publică și în infrastructurile critice ar trebui să fie supuse unor audituri independente înainte de implementare și unor evaluări periodice după punerea în funcțiune.

Europa are nevoie de un mecanism comun de alertă și schimb rapid de informații privind incidentele cibernetice și vulnerabilitățile IA, deoarece timpul este adesea mai important decât resursele.

O altă prioritate este investiția în oameni. Deficitul de specialiști în securitate cibernetică devine o vulnerabilitate strategică. Avem nevoie de programe europene de formare, de exerciții comune și de o mai bună circulație a expertizei între statele membre.

Nu putem ignora nici impactul asupra democrației. IA face posibilă producerea la scară industrială a conținutului manipulator, a atacurilor informaționale și a campaniilor de dezinformare. Reziliența democratică trebuie să facă parte din politica europeană de securitate cibernetică.

Autonomia tehnologică nu este un slogan. Dacă infrastructura digitală a Europei depinde de tehnologii pe care nu le controlăm, vulnerabilitatea noastră rămâne structurală. Acesta este motivul pentru care investiția în capacități europene trebuie să devină o prioritate strategică.

discussion.text: Los socialistas hemos subrayado que Europa debe reforzar su soberanía tecnológica en inteligencia artificial y ciberseguridad. Aunque se valora el plan de acción sobre ciberseguridad e inteligencia artificial de la Comisión Europea, desde el Grupo S&D hemos señalado que la regulación no es suficiente: es necesario aumentar la inversión pública, apoyar a las empresas europeas y aplicar medidas efectivas para garantizar la seguridad, lo que incluye el cumplimiento de normativas como la Directiva SRI 2. We have also warned about new threats, such as quantum computing, and underlined the importance of protecting not only critical infrastructure but also citizens—especially minors—against the risks of artificial intelligence.

Exactly, by the way, the same week that Donald Trump has acknowledged that his sons —who are engaged in manufacturing military drones— have had access to privileged information about Donald Trump's decisions. I suppose they will also have had access to information on how Trump imposes decisions on this submissive Europe, on this submissive Europe regarding US imperialism.

That is all you offer Europeans, on the part of the European Commission: war, a further increase in military spending, submission and a lot of power for the...

discussion.speaker: Michael GAHLER
discussion.text:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Die Ukraine und die Ukrainer sind auf dem Weg in die Europäische Union. Dieser Weg ist unwiderruflich, weil die Ukrainer das wollen und weil auch wir das wollen. Es ist im beiderseitigen Interesse, dass diese europäische Nation ihren Platz in der Gemeinschaft der freien Völker Europas findet. Das imperialistische Russland, das von einem Mann geführt wird, der nach Hitler und Stalin die drittgrößten Verbrechen der europäischen Neuzeit begeht, an Ukrainern und am eigenen Volk, wird das nicht verhindern. Russland wird historisch scheitern, wenn die Ukraine auf dem Weg in die EU ist.

Das erste Cluster von Verhandlungskapiteln ist eröffnet. Ich finde, es wäre ein gutes Signal, auch die anderen idealerweise beim nächsten Europäischen Rat mit zu eröffnen. Das kürzt nichts ab; das ersetzt nicht die Notwendigkeit, die Voraussetzungen für den Beitritt inhaltlich zu erfüllen. Es wäre aber ein weiteres deutliches Signal an Ukrainer, EU‑Bürger und den Aggressor Russland, dass es keinen Weg zurück in den sowjetischen Gulag, sondern vorwärts in eine gemeinsame europäische Zukunft gibt.

In diesem Bericht, der im Wesentlichen von fünf Fraktionen und darüber hinaus einer Anzahl weiterer Abgeordneter getragen wird, machen wir deutlich, wo die Ukraine auf dem Weg in die EU steht. Wir haben hierzu eine Vielzahl von Quellen genutzt, vor allem aber auch den Dialog praktiziert mit den politisch Verantwortlichen in Kyjiw, in den Regionen bis hin zur kommunalen Ebene, und natürlich mit unseren eigenen Vertretern vor Ort und in Brüssel und mit der starken und beeindruckend kompetenten ukrainischen Zivilgesellschaft.

Daraus ergibt sich ein klares Bild, was zu tun ist. Alle Institutionen, die für den Rechtsstaat relevant sind, müssen gestärkt bzw. reformiert werden. Das heißt, die Antikorruptionsbehörden müssen ihre Arbeit unabhängig verrichten können. Die obersten Gerichte müssen nach einem transparenten Auswahlprozess besetzt werden. Absolventen der Universitäten, die die Befähigung zum Richteramt erworben haben, müssen von unten die Richterschaft erneuern. Die Generalstaatsanwaltschaft hat nicht die Aufgabe, Weisungen an die Antikorruptionsbehörden zu erteilen. Der Geheimdienst muss Staatsfeinde bekämpfen. Die Antikorruptionsbehörden sind keine Staatsfeinde, sondern bekämpfen diejenigen, die ein falsches Staatsverständnis haben; es kann daher nicht Aufgabe des Geheimdienstes sein, Antikorruptionsbehörden auszuforschen. Ein State Bureau of Investigation sollte nicht ein Bezirksgericht anrufen, um zu verhindern, dass das Ergebnis einer journalistischen Investigativrecherche veröffentlicht wird, die den Bruder des Direktors betrifft. Gewählte Politiker sind keine öffentlichen Angestellten; für sie gilt kein Beamtenrecht; sie können daher auch nicht mit Maßnahmen des Beamtenrechts sanktioniert werden; die freie Mandatsausübung ist auch in Kriegszeiten ein hohes Gut.

Da für alle Parteien in der Werchowna Rada neben dem EU‑Beitrittsprozess die Bekämpfung des Aggressors Russland an erster Stelle steht, rate ich an, innenpolitische Auseinandersetzungen oder taktische Spielchen auf die Zeit nach dem Ende der Kampfhandlungen und die Vorbereitung auf Wahlen zu konzentrieren und stattdessen gemeinsam gegen den Aggressor zu stehen.

Und hier kommt noch mal der Beitrittsprozess ins Spiel: Wir müssen uns klarmachen, dass neben dem traditionellen merit-based approach, also einem Fortschritt entsprechend der Erfüllung des acquis, eine geopolitische Dimension hinzutritt, und die ist zunehmend auch in unserem Interesse. Es ist die Ukraine, die uns die Zeit verschafft, gegenüber der Bedrohung durch den Aggressor Russland verteidigungsfähig zu werden. Die Ukrainer sind derzeit die einzigen, die Russland aufhalten können.

Daraus ergibt sich eine Gesamtschau, die die Ukrainer und uns zusammenführt in dem Interesse, gemeinsam nach dem Ende des Kriegszustands beide Prozesse zu gestalten – den EU‑Beitritt und eine gegenseitige Sicherheitsgarantie, dass wir auch vor einer EU‑ oder NATO‑Mitgliedschaft füreinander einstehen. Keine direkte, aber eine entsprechende Anwendung des Artikels 42 Absatz 7, die nicht nur für uns gegenüber der Ukraine, sondern auch für die Ukraine uns gegenüber gilt. Nur gemeinsam sind wir stark genug. Slawa Europa! Slawa Ukrajini!

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues! Ukraine and the Ukrainians are on their way into the European Union. This path is irrevocable because the Ukrainians want it and because we want it too. It is in our mutual interest that this European nation finds its place in the community of free peoples of Europe. Imperialist Russia, led by a man who, after Hitler and Stalin, is committing the third-largest crimes of modern European history against Ukrainians and his own people, will not prevent this. Russia will fail historically when Ukraine is on the path to the EU.

The first cluster of negotiation chapters is open. I think it would be a good signal to ideally open the others at the next European Council as well. That does not cut corners; it does not replace the necessity to fulfill the prerequisites for accession in terms of content. However, it would be another clear signal to Ukrainians, EU citizens, and the aggressor Russia that there is no way back into the Soviet Gulag, but rather forward into a shared European future.

In this report, which is supported essentially by five political groups and a number of other Members beyond that, we make clear where Ukraine stands on its way to the EU. To this end, we have used a multitude of sources, but above all we have practiced dialogue with those politically responsible in Kyiv, in the regions down to the municipal level, and of course with our own representatives on the ground and in Brussels, and with the strong and impressively competent Ukrainian civil society.

This paints a clear picture of what needs to be done. All institutions relevant to the rule of law must be strengthened or reformed. That means anti-corruption agencies must be able to carry out their work independently. The supreme courts must be staffed following a transparent selection process. University graduates who have qualified for judicial office must renew the judiciary from the bottom up. The Prosecutor General's Office does not have the task of issuing instructions to the anti-corruption agencies. The secret service must fight enemies of the state. Anti-corruption agencies are not enemies of the state, but rather fight those who have a false understanding of the state; it can therefore not be the task of the secret service to spy on anti-corruption agencies. A State Bureau of Investigation should not appeal to a district court to prevent the publication of the result of an investigative journalistic report concerning the director's brother. Elected politicians are not public employees; civil service law does not apply to them; they therefore cannot be sanctioned with civil service law measures; the free exercise of a mandate is a high good even in times of war.

Since for all parties in the Verkhovna Rada, alongside the EU accession process, fighting the aggressor Russia is the top priority, I advise concentrating domestic political disputes or tactical games on the time after the end of hostilities and the preparation for elections, and instead standing together against the aggressor.

And here the accession process comes into play once again: we must realize that alongside the traditional merit-based approach—that is, progress in accordance with the fulfillment of the acquis—a geopolitical dimension is being added, and this is increasingly in our interest as well. It is Ukraine that is buying us the time to become capable of defending ourselves against the threat posed by the aggressor Russia. The Ukrainians are currently the only ones who can stop Russia.

This results in an overall perspective that brings the Ukrainians and us together in the interest of jointly shaping both processes after the end of the state of war—EU accession and a mutual security guarantee that we will stand up for each other even before EU or NATO membership. Not a direct, but a corresponding application of Article 42 Paragraph 7, which applies not only from us toward Ukraine, but also from Ukraine toward us. Only together are we strong enough. Slawa Europa! Slawa Ukrajini!

discussion.speaker: Marta Kos
discussion.text:
Mr President, honourable Members, thank you, dear rapporteur, Michael Gahler, for your report and for your engagement on Ukraine at a time when Russia is intensifying its attacks against Ukraine. As it struggles to achieve its objectives on the battlefield, it is important to remember what this war is ultimately about. This is not only a war over territory. It is a war about Ukraine's right to choose its own future – a sovereign nation that has chosen democracy, has chosen Europe, and has chosen the path towards membership of the European Union. That is a choice Moscow does not accept. Ukraine's European future is about the security, stability and prosperity of our entire continent.

Just two weeks ago, at the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdańsk, I met with Ukrainian defence companies. I saw first‑hand an industry that is producing some of the world's most advanced drones at remarkable speed and with an extraordinary capacity for innovation. This is why we are deepening cooperation between the European and Ukrainian defence industries. Ukraine is already facilitating exports of military technologies to the European Union, and this cooperation will continue to expand.

For example, through the Ukraine investment framework, we have also started promoting joint projects with Member States by providing guarantees that support dual‑use production, helping to integrate our industrial bases and strengthen Europe's defence readiness. Ukraine has become a fundamental pillar of Europe's security architecture. The courage of the Ukrainian people and their military innovation are already strengthening Europe's security today, and this brings me to enlargement.

Security and enlargement cannot be seen as two separate agendas. They are two sides of the same coin. A stronger, more secure Europe requires a credible enlargement policy, and a credible enlargement policy strengthens our collective security. We must get this right. That is why the accession process will remain rigorous, fair and firmly merit based. This principle is not negotiable. Over the past years, Ukraine has maintained a consistent reform trajectory and continued aligning with the EU acquis. Across all the negotiating chapters, we have seen no backsliding or stagnation. Good or some progress has been recorded in 27 out of 33 chapters assessed. This reflects sustained political commitment under exceptionally difficult circumstances.

At the same time, further efforts remain necessary. Particularly on the fundamentals, Ukraine must continue strengthening the fight against corruption, as you have said, upholding the rule of law, ensuring the effective functioning of democratic institutions and advancing public administration reform. I have made this clear in all my exchanges with the Ukrainian authorities, Parliament and also civil society. The interim benchmarks for the rule of law for cluster one, together with the roadmaps adopted last year, provide a solid framework to guide these reforms. The Commission will continue to monitor progress closely and provide the support needed to maintain reform momentum.

The opening of the first cluster on 15 June was an important milestone and, for many in the Hall at that time, very emotional. It demonstrated the actual progress is possible when reforms deliver results. Our objective should now be to open the remaining negotiating clusters as soon as possible, building on the extensive preparatory work already undertaken. At the same time, while Ukraine advances on its accession path, we should continue exploring every possible avenue for gradual integration, for instance under the Association Agreement, enabling Ukraine and its citizens to benefit progressively from closer integration with the Union even before accession is completed.

Honourable Members, we should not forget the bigger picture and have it all the time inside. Ukraine's accession is an investment in a stronger, safer and resilient Europe. It is not just about Ukraine: it is also about us. So let us remain united and continue walking this path together with Ukraine. This can only be for the benefit of Ukraine, for the benefit of the EU and for the security of all us Europeans.

discussion.speaker: Andrzej HALICKI
discussion.text:
Panie Przewodniczący! Wszyscy chcemy, żeby Ukraina wygrała z Putinem. Zbrodnicza rosyjska armia napadła na Ukrainę dlatego, że Ukraińcy chcą europejskiej przyszłości dla swojego kraju. I my chcemy Ukrainy europejskiej. Chcemy i wierzymy, że to może się zdarzyć. Do tego potrzebne są oczywiście konsekwentne działania. Dlatego tak ważne są reformy, tak ważne jest oparcie państwa na praworządności, na prawdziwej, realnej, konsekwentnej walce z korupcją, bo żadne euro nie może być przekazane i zdefraudowane.

Ale także niezbędne jest poszanowanie wspólnych europejskich wartości, bo nie można we Wspólnocie gloryfikować tych, którzy opierali swoją przeszłość, swoją aktywność na walce z mniejszościami, na działaniach o charakterze ludobójczym. Jeżeli przypominamy ten fakt jako Parlament Europejski, przypominamy to po to, by jeszcze raz powiedzieć jedno przesłanie: to wy wybieracie swoją przyszłość. Ale jeżeli chcecie być we Wspólnocie, musicie szanować te wartości, które opisane są w art. 2, i rzeczywiście promować to, co jest naszą wspólną europejską zasadą.

Nie ma miejsca na gloryfikowanie zbrodniarzy. Żadne euro nie może być wydane na te oddziały, które mają imię zbrodniarzy odpowiedzialnych za ludobójstwo. Europejska przyszłość leży w waszych rękach.

translation.englishText:
Mr President! We all want Ukraine to win against Putin. The criminal Russian army attacked Ukraine because Ukrainians want a European future for their country. And we want a European Ukraine. We want and believe that this can happen. Of course, consistent action is needed for this. That is why reforms are so important, why it is so important to base the state on the rule of law, on a real, genuine, consistent fight against corruption, because no euro can be transferred and embezzled.

But it is also necessary to respect common European values, because in the Community one cannot glorify those who based their past, their activity on the fight against minorities, on genocidal actions. If we recall this fact as the European Parliament, we recall it to state one message once again: you choose your future. But if you want to be in the Community, you must respect those values that are described in Article 2 and truly promote what is our common European principle.

There is no room for glorifying criminals. No euro can be spent on those units that bear the name of criminals responsible for genocide. The European future lies in your hands.
translation.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Wszyscy chcemy, żeby Ukraina wygrała z Putinem. Zbrodnicza rosyjska armia napadła na Ukrainę dlatego, że Ukraińcy chcą europejskiej przyszłości dla swojego kraju. I my chcemy Ukrainy europejskiej. Chcemy i wierzymy, że to może się zdarzyć. Do tego potrzebne są oczywiście konsekwentne działania. Dlatego tak ważne są reformy, tak ważne jest oparcie państwa na praworządności, na prawdziwej, realnej, konsekwentnej walce z korupcją, bo żadne euro nie może być przekazane i zdefraudowane.

Ale także niezbędne jest poszanowanie wspólnych europejskich wartości, bo nie można we Wspólnocie gloryfikować tych, którzy opierali swoją przeszłość, swoją aktywność na walce z mniejszościami, na działaniach o charakterze ludobójczym. Ale jeżeli chcecie być we Wspólnocie, musicie szanować te wartości, które opisane są w art. 2, i rzeczywiście promować to, co jest naszą wspólną europejską zasadą.

Nie ma miejsca na gloryfikowanie zbrodniarzy. Żadne euro nie może być wydane na te oddziały, które mają imię zbrodniarzy odpowiedzialnych za ludobójstwo. Europejska przyszłość leży w waszych rękach.

discussion.speaker: Thijs REUTEN
discussion.text:
Mr President, Ukraine is squeezing the Russian economy. It regains territory, despite dire front-line conditions. Putin is lashing out with deadly strikes on cities where air defence ammunition has run out.

Europe needs four things now more than ever: vigilance, focus, unity and resolve.

Vigilance: we need vigilance because Russia wants to break our support for Ukraine. Further probing, a false flag, stoking bilateral disputes to split our unity – even a minor incursion. Let us signal clearly that the cost of any probe or incursion will be catastrophic, almost non-European, and it will only bring more backing for Ukraine.

Focus: we need focus because Member States must stop ignoring accession non-papers, and start empowering Ukraine's EU membership. That means backing reforms, making accession a truly credible perspective with immediate interim steps, proving there is no turning back, and also a clear trajectory to the finish line. It also includes building a security architecture with Ukraine rooted in our shared future.

Unity: because Europe must act and speak as one – on accession, on defence support, on the shadow fleet, on banning any dual-use exports, on peace talks. Our report calls for a European negotiator to protect our interests and help defend Ukraine and end Russia's war, not to normalise relations. There can be no normalisation without respect for Ukraine's territorial integrity, without justice, accountability and reparations, and without an end to Russia's hybrid war on Europe.

And finally, resolve: as long as our response to Russia killing civilians is broken, allow me to be a broken record. Air defence, deep strike capabilities and jointly operated sky shields – they save Ukrainian lives. Our statements do not. Europe must be unwavering in words and deeds.

discussion.speaker: António TÂNGER CORRÊA
discussion.text:
Mr. President, Commissioner, I'm speaking Portuguese.

Estamos, sem hesitações, ao lado do povo ucraniano, ao lado das mães que perderam filhos, de um povo que viu a sua terra invadida, as suas cidades destruídas e o seu futuro suspenso. A agressão russa deve ser condenada com toda a clareza, como a condenaríamos se se tratasse do nosso próprio país.

A soberania e a independência da Ucrânia não podem ser moeda de troca, e nenhuma paz pode ser negociada sem a Ucrânia. Mas estar com a Ucrânia é também dizer a verdade. O melhor para a Ucrânia não é uma guerra sem fim. O melhor é uma paz justa, segura e duradoura, uma paz que chegue quanto antes.

E também temos de dizer a verdade aos portugueses: esta guerra entrou nas casas portuguesas pela fatura da energia, pelo preço dos combustíveis, pela inflação, pela perda do poder de compra e pela erosão silenciosa da sua qualidade de vida.

O dinheiro europeu para a Ucrânia tem de ser escrutinado, não pode ser um cheque em branco. Já se descobriram desvios de fundos europeus na Ucrânia de mais de 90 milhões de EUR. Temos o dever de proteger os nossos contribuintes e garantir que cada euro chega ao seu destino.

Mas o problema não é apenas o mérito na entrada da Ucrânia para a União Europeia, é também o impacto. Qual será o impacto na vida da coesão, nos pequenos países como Portugal, na agricultura, nos transportes, na energia, na indústria, no mercado interno e nos sectores críticos das nossas economias?

Não pode haver exceção. Os critérios de Copenhaga têm de ser absolutamente cumpridos.

A Europa deve apoiar a Ucrânia, sim, mas deve fazê-lo com seriedade, não com irresponsabilidade. Ninguém tem o direito de decidir isto com leviandade. Ninguém tem o direito de sacrificar a coesão europeia nem de fragilizar os pequenos Estados para alimentar gestos simbólicos ou calendários políticos.

translation.englishText:
Mr. President, Commissioner, I'm speaking Portuguese.

We stand, without hesitation, alongside the Ukrainian people, alongside mothers who have lost sons, a people who saw their land invaded, their cities destroyed, and their future suspended. Russian aggression must be condemned with all clarity, as we would condemn it if it were our own country.

The sovereignty and independence of Ukraine cannot be a bargaining chip, and no peace can be negotiated without Ukraine. But standing with Ukraine also means telling the truth. The best thing for Ukraine is not an endless war. The best thing is a just, secure, and lasting peace, a peace that arrives as soon as possible.

And we also have to tell the truth to the Portuguese: this war has entered Portuguese homes through energy bills, fuel prices, inflation, the loss of purchasing power, and the silent erosion of their quality of life.

European money for Ukraine must be scrutinized, it cannot be a blank check. Misappropriations of European funds in Ukraine of more than 90 million EUR have already been discovered. We have a duty to protect our taxpayers and ensure that every euro reaches its destination.

But the problem is not only the merit of Ukraine's entry into the European Union, it is also the impact. What will be the impact on the life of cohesion, on small countries like Portugal, on agriculture, on transport, on energy, on industry, on the internal market, and on the critical sectors of our economies?

There can be no exception. The Copenhagen criteria must be absolutely fulfilled.

Europe must support Ukraine, yes, but it must do so with seriousness, not with irresponsibility. No one has the right to decide this lightly. No one has the right to sacrifice European cohesion nor to weaken small States to feed symbolic gestures or political calendars.

discussion.speaker: Michał DWORCZYK
discussion.text:
Panie Przewodniczący! Od pierwszego dnia rosyjskiej agresji wspieramy Ukrainę politycznie, militarnie i humanitarnie, ponieważ jej niestrudzona walka z rosyjskim reżimem stanowi dzisiaj ważny filar bezpieczeństwa całej Europy. Polacy pozostają w tym procesie narodem, który okazał największe zaangażowanie i wsparcie.

Z drugiej strony, europejskie aspiracje Ukrainy oraz rozpoczęte negocjacje akcesyjne są niewątpliwie źródłem nadziei milionów Ukraińców na europejską przyszłość Ukrainy. Należy docenić reformy i zmiany w prawie implementowane na Ukrainie, których celem jest realizacja europejskich standardów.

Jednak europejska integracja oznacza nie tylko dostosowanie prawa krajowego, lecz także wierność podstawowym wartościom, na których zbudowana jest Unia Europejska, w tym prawdzie historycznej, szacunku dla ofiar oraz odwadze w mierzeniu się z własną, nawet najcięższą przeszłością. Dlatego absolutnie jako nieakceptowalną przyjęliśmy decyzję o nadaniu elitarnej jednostce Sił Zbrojnych Ukrainy imienia „bohaterów UPA”, formacji odpowiedzialnej za wymordowanie około 100 tysięcy cywilów, głównie polskich kobiet i dzieci, choć wśród ofiar znaleźli się również Żydzi, Czesi oraz Ukraińcy ratujący swoich sąsiadów.

Nie może być zgody na gloryfikację i nawiązywanie do organizacji oraz środowisk odpowiedzialnych za zbrodnie wojenne, takich jak 14. Dywizja Grenadierów SS Galizien, batalion „Nachtigall” czy batalion „Roland”. Decyzja prezydenta Zełenskiego zbezcześciła pamięć wszystkich ofiar ludobójstwa dokonanego na terenie południowo-wschodnich województw II Rzeczypospolitej przez ukraińskich nacjonalistów.

Pojednanie wymaga prawdy. Ukraina powinna jednoznacznie potępić ideologię UPA, która doprowadziła do masowych zbrodni, oraz umożliwić pełne ekshumacje i godny pochówek wszystkich ofiar. Prawda historyczna nie jest przeszkodą dla pojednania, nie jest przeszkodą w drodze do Europy. Wręcz odwrotnie, jest jej fundamentem. Tylko na fundamencie prawdy i wzajemnego szacunku możemy budować wspólną europejską przyszłość.

translation.englishText:
Mr President! From the very first day of Russian aggression, we have supported Ukraine politically, militarily, and humanitarianly, because its tireless fight against the Russian regime currently constitutes an important pillar of security for the whole of Europe. Poles remain the nation in this process that has shown the greatest commitment and support.

On the other hand, Ukraine's European aspirations and the initiated accession negotiations are undoubtedly a source of hope for millions of Ukrainians regarding Ukraine's European future. The reforms and legislative changes implemented in Ukraine aimed at achieving European standards must be appreciated.

However, European integration means not only the alignment of national law, but also fidelity to the core values upon which the European Union is built, including historical truth, respect for victims, and the courage to confront one's own, even the heaviest, past. Therefore, we found completely unacceptable the decision to name an elite unit of the Armed Forces of Ukraine after the "Heroes of the UPA", a formation responsible for the murder of approximately 100,000 civilians, mostly Polish women and children, although the victims also included Jews, Czechs, and Ukrainians who saved their neighbours.

There can be no consent to the glorification of and reference to organisations and circles responsible for war crimes, such as the 14th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS Galicia, the Nachtigall Battalion, or the Roland Battalion. President Zelenskyy's decision desecrated the memory of all victims of the genocide committed in the south-eastern voivodeships of the Second Polish Republic by Ukrainian nationalists.

Reconciliation requires truth. Ukraine should unequivocally condemn the UPA ideology that led to mass crimes, and enable full exhumations and a dignified burial of all victims. Historical truth is not an obstacle to reconciliation, nor is it an obstacle on the path to Europe. On the contrary, it is its foundation. Only on the foundation of truth and mutual respect can we build a common European future.

discussion.speaker: Petras AUŠTREVIČIUS
discussion.text:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Ukraine's integration into the EU offers guarantees for its sovereignty and endurance. Ultimately, it would significantly reinforce Europe's security. It is a mutually beneficial win‑win situation. Negotiations on Ukraine's membership should begin as soon as possible, covering all six negotiation chapters and clusters, while maintaining high standards and ensuring compliance with all conditions.

Russia, the aggressor, is doing and will continue to do everything in its power to weaken Ukraine, terrorise its brave people and delay the prospects of the European future. As partners and allies, we must support Ukraine in its fight for survival. Europe's support for Ukraine is the ultimate test for European leadership today.

The recent tensions between Poland and Ukraine, rooted in complex historical grievances, must be resolved as soon as possible, while avoiding the rise of nationalism and historical hegemony. Europe's strength lies in unity.

discussion.speaker: Villy SØVNDAL
discussion.text:
Hr. formand! Jeg og kollegerne fra Parlamentet er netop kommet hjem fra et besøg i Ukraine, hvor vi så og hørte om konsekvenserne af de massive terrorbombninger af civilbefolkningen.

Men samtidig er Ukraine også et land, hvor vi ser glimt af håb, jeg ikke har oplevet i løbet af krigens forløb. Vi ser det ved fronten, hvor ukrainerne vinder initiativet mod syd, mens russerne stadig væk presser på mod øst. Vi ser det, når det ukrainske militær slår tilbage mod energi og militære strategiske mål langt inde i Rusland og dermed svækker både den russiske økonomi, men også deres militær. Vi ser det også, når Putins regime mister fodfæste. Putins løgne om krigens årsag og krigens gang er begyndt at sætte spor i den russiske befolkning.

Vi er ved et afgørende øjeblik. Derfor skal EU og medlemslandene ikke alene fastholde, men styrke hjælpen til Ukraine, så Putin tvinges til at respektere de internationalt anerkendte grænser. Tyrannen og vanviddet må og skal stoppes!

translation.englishText:
Mr President! My colleagues from Parliament and I have just returned home from a visit to Ukraine, where we saw and heard about the consequences of the massive terror bombings of the civilian population.

At the same time, however, Ukraine is also a country where we see glimpses of hope that I have not experienced during the course of the war. We see it at the front, where the Ukrainians are winning the initiative to the south, while the Russians are still pressing on to the east. We see it when the Ukrainian military strikes back against energy and military strategic targets deep inside Russia, thereby weakening both the Russian economy and their military. We also see it when Putin's regime is losing its footing. Putin's lies about the cause of the war and the course of the war have begun to leave their mark on the Russian population.

We are at a decisive moment. Therefore, the EU and the member states must not only maintain, but strengthen the aid to Ukraine, so that Putin is forced to respect the internationally recognized borders. The tyrant and the madness must and shall be stopped!

discussion.speaker: Özlem DEMIREL
discussion.text:
Herr Präsident! Es ist wieder soweit – der Jahresbericht zur Ukraine. Alle Jahre wieder sprechen Sie hier vor allem über Waffen, Aufrüstung und geopolitische Interessen, aber viel zu selten sprechen Sie über die Menschen, über eine Friedensperspektive. Seit über vier Jahren leben Millionen Menschen in der Ukraine im Krieg; Arbeiterinnen und Arbeiter verlieren ihre Existenz; soziale Rechte und Gewerkschaften stehen unter Druck. Die Regierung Selenskyj steht wegen Korruption und Angriffen auf soziale Rechte in der Kritik, gleichzeitig wird der Ausverkauf des Landes vorangetrieben.

Doch über diese Realitäten reden Sie nicht gerne. Stattdessen feiern Sie neue Waffen und Drohnentechnologien, als wäre Krieg ein Spiel. Aber die Folge dieser Eskalation tragen nicht Sie hier – die tragen die Menschen vor Ort. Ihre Antwort bleibt immer dieselbe: mehr Waffen, mehr Aufrüstung, mehr Militarisierung. Und dieser Bericht spricht erneut über Taurus-Lieferungen.

Während immer mehr Menschen in der Ukraine und in Russland versuchen, diesem Krieg zu entkommen, soll nun sogar der Schutz ukrainischer Geflüchteter der Kriegsfähigkeit der Ukraine untergeordnet werden. Männer im wehrfähigen Alter sollen zurückgewiesen werden; Männer sollen damit zur militärischen Ressource gemacht werden. Das ist zynisch. Menschen sind keine Waffen; Kriegsdienstverweigerung ist ein Menschenrecht.

Auch der Beitrittsprozess wird mitten im Krieg geopolitischen Interessen untergeordnet. Solidarität bedeutet nicht, einen Krieg endlos zu verlängern. Solidarität bedeutet Schutz für Menschen, soziale Rechte und einen Wiederaufbau im Interesse der Menschen. Europa braucht keine Eskalation, sondern den Weg zum Frieden.

translation.englishText:
Mr President! Here we go again – the annual report on Ukraine. Year after year, you talk here primarily about weapons, rearmament and geopolitical interests, but far too rarely do you talk about the people, about a perspective for peace. For over four years, millions of people have been living in war in Ukraine; workers are losing their livelihoods; social rights and trade unions are under pressure. The Zelenskyy government is facing criticism for corruption and attacks on social rights, while the sell-out of the country is being driven forward.

Yet you do not like talking about these realities. Instead, you celebrate new weapons and drone technologies as if war were a game. But the consequences of this escalation are not borne by you here – they are borne by the people on the ground. Your answer always remains the same: more weapons, more rearmament, more militarisation. And this report once again talks about Taurus deliveries.

While more and more people in Ukraine and in Russia are trying to escape this war, the protection of Ukrainian refugees is now even to be subordinated to Ukraine's war-fighting capability. Men of military age are to be turned away; men are thereby to be made into a military resource. That is cynical. People are not weapons; conscientious objection is a human right.

The accession process, too, is being subordinated to geopolitical interests in the middle of the war. Solidarity does not mean endlessly prolonging a war. Solidarity means protection for people, social rights and reconstruction in the interest of the people. Europe does not need escalation, but the path to peace.

discussion.factCheck: The claim that Ukraine has failed to meet any of the core criteria for joining the European Union is false; the EU granted Ukraine candidate status in 2022, officially opened accession negotiations in 2024, and opened the first negotiating cluster on 'Fundamentals' in June 2026, repeatedly recognizing the country's progress in implementing key reforms.
discussion.speaker: Petar VOLGIN
discussion.text:
Господин Председател, pъководителите в Киев носят главната отговорност за това Украйна да не е изпълнила нито един от основните критерии за влизане в Европейския съюз. Най-близките приятели и сътрудници на Владимир Зеленски са обвинени, че са създали корупционни схеми за присвояването на огромни суми пари.

Представяте ли си какво ще направят тези хора или други подобни с европейските средства, ако страната им все пак влезе в Европейския съюз? Ако това присъединяване наистина се случи, ще имаме държава - член на Евросъюза, в която няма независими медии, няма свобода на словото, няма и политически плурализъм. Властите в Киев в момента провеждат активна политика по възвеличаването на хора, които активно са участвали в нацистките престъпления през Втората световна война. Личности и организации, отговорни за престъпления срещу човечеството, днес там се честват като герои, а Евросъюзът винаги категорично е осъждал подобни чудовищни деяния. Ето защо държавни ръководители, които се прекланят пред нацистки престъпници, няма как да преговарят за членство в Европейския съюз. А напоследък властите в Киев правят всичко възможно, за да забранят официално и украинската православна църква, просто защото тя не желае да се подчинява на диктата им.

Изобщо днешната власт в Киев е олицетворение на всичко това, срещу което Европейският съюз твърди, че се бори, Тя е корумпирана, унищожава свободата, величае нацизма и принуждава милиони украинци да търсят спасение в чужбина. Ако Брюксел допусне такива управляващи в Европейския съюз, той без съмнение ще спечели Световното първенство по лицемерие.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, the leaders in Kyiv bear the main responsibility for Ukraine having failed to meet any of the core criteria for joining the European Union. Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s closest friends and associates are accused of having created corruption schemes for the embezzlement of huge sums of money.

Can you imagine what these people or others like them will do with European funds if their country nonetheless enters the European Union? If this accession really happens, we will have a member state of the European Union in which there are no independent media, no freedom of speech, and no political pluralism. The authorities in Kyiv are currently pursuing an active policy of glorifying individuals who actively participated in Nazi crimes during the Second World War. Figures and organizations responsible for crimes against humanity are celebrated there today as heroes, and the European Union has always firmly condemned such monstrous acts. That is why state leaders who bow before Nazi criminals have no business negotiating membership in the European Union. And lately, the authorities in Kyiv are doing everything possible to officially ban the Ukrainian Orthodox Church simply because it does not wish to obey their dictate.

Altogether, today’s government in Kyiv is the personification of everything that the European Union claims to fight against. It is corrupt, destroys freedom, glorifies Nazism, and forces millions of Ukrainians to seek salvation abroad. If Brussels admits such rulers into the European Union, it will undoubtedly win the World Cup of hypocrisy.
translation.factCheck: The claim that Ukraine has failed to meet any of the core criteria for joining the European Union is false; the EU granted Ukraine candidate status in 2022, officially opened accession negotiations in 2024, and opened the first negotiating cluster on 'Fundamentals' in June 2026, repeatedly recognizing the country's progress in implementing key reforms.
