discussion.speaker: Georgiana TEODORESCU
discussion.text:
Domnule președinte, suntem cu toții de acord că locul Moldovei este în Uniunea Europeană. Sunt frații noștri, ai românilor, vorbesc limba română, sunt creștini ortodocși majoritatea și împărtășesc același trecut și aceleași valori cu România, stat membru UE. Când și cum se va face această aderare? Aici este adevărata cheia a acestei dezbateri.

Prima, cea mai rapidă și firească totodată, ar fi soluția germană, despre care eu și colegii mei din partid am tot vorbit. A doua variantă, aderarea propriu-zisă, trebuie făcută pe un calendar propriu, independent de Ucraina. Moldova are propriul ei drum și propria ei viteză de îndeplinire a condițiilor pentru aderare la UE. Deci nu există niciun motiv să o tratăm la pachet cu Ucraina.

În plus, Ucraina este, din păcate, o țară aflată încă în război cu teritoriul disputat, deci nu putem vorbi de aderare efectivă în acest stadiu. Și ar fi nedrept să susținem și Moldova blocată la pachet cu ea. Orice țară care dorește să adere la UE trebuie să îndeplinească fix aceleași condiții ca și antemergători ei, iar din acest punct de vedere trebuie să spunem clar: Moldova se află cu mulți pași înaintea Ucrainei, deci cu mulți pași mai aproape de Uniunea Europeană.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, we all agree that Moldova's place is in the European Union. They are our brothers, the brothers of Romanians, they speak the Romanian language, the majority are Orthodox Christians and they share the same past and the same values with Romania, an EU member state. When and how will this accession take place? Here is the true key to this debate.

The first, and at the same time the fastest and most natural solution, would be the German solution, which I and my party colleagues have been talking about. The second option, actual accession, must be done on its own calendar, independent of Ukraine. Moldova has its own path and its own speed for fulfilling the conditions for EU accession. So there is no reason to treat it bundled together with Ukraine.

In addition, Ukraine is, unfortunately, a country still at war with disputed territory, so we cannot talk about effective accession at this stage. And it would be unfair to keep Moldova blocked bundled together with it. Any country that wants to accede to the EU must meet the exact same conditions as its predecessors, and from this point of view we must say it clearly: Moldova is many steps ahead of Ukraine, and therefore many steps closer to the European Union.

discussion.speaker: Nathalie LOISEAU
discussion.text:
Monsieur le Président, ainsi donc, les négociations d’adhésion s’ouvrent enfin avec la Moldavie: il était temps! Le peuple moldave l’a dit, redit et le répète encore: il se sent européen, il veut entrer dans l’Union européenne. Il a voté en ce sens à plusieurs reprises, en dépit des pressions insensées que la Russie a fait peser sur lui. Manipulation de l’information, achats de voix, oligarques à la botte de Moscou, gangs criminels, pressions économiques: la petite Moldavie a eu droit à tout et a résisté à tout.

On la regarde parfois avec condescendance: on ferait mieux d’en prendre de la graine. Parce que des manipulations de l’information, des groupes de médias étrangers bienveillants vis-à-vis de Vladimir Poutine et des tentatives d’intimidation, eh bien ça ne se passe pas qu’en Moldavie.

Le peuple moldave veut rejoindre l’Union européenne, et ses autorités savent ce qu’elles ont à faire, les réformes qu’elles ont à mener pour y parvenir. Mais nous, est-ce que nous savons ce que nous voulons? Sommes-nous prêts à accueillir de nouveaux membres dans notre Union? J’ai bien peur que nous n’ayons pas encore pris la mesure du monde qui nous entoure.

L’élargissement de l’Union européenne peut être une chance: celle d’échapper à notre encerclement. Mais sa réussite va dépendre aussi de nous.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, so accession negotiations are finally opening with Moldova: it was about time! The Moldovan people have said it, said it again and are repeating it: they feel European, they want to join the European Union. They have voted to this effect on several occasions, despite the insane pressure that Russia has exerted on them. Information manipulation, vote-buying, oligarchs at Moscow’s beck and call, criminal gangs, economic pressure: little Moldova has faced it all and resisted it all.

It is sometimes looked down upon with condescension: we would do better to take a leaf out of its book. Because information manipulation, foreign media groups well-disposed towards Vladimir Putin and attempts at intimidation, well, that doesn’t only happen in Moldova.

The Moldovan people want to join the European Union, and its authorities know what they have to do, the reforms they have to carry out to achieve this. But do we know what we want? Are we ready to welcome new members into our Union? I am very much afraid that we have not yet grasped the measure of the world around us.

Enlargement of the European Union can be an opportunity: that of escaping our encirclement. But its success will also depend on us.

discussion.speaker: Reinhold LOPATKA
discussion.text:
Mr President, dear colleagues, Russia's brutal war of aggression has shown that there are no grey zones on our continent, no place for grey zones. We must therefore continue supporting all enlargement countries who are demonstrating willingness to progress on the path of EU integration.

Moldova has shown a strong determination in the implementation of reforms, in the face of challenging circumstances, despite disinformation campaigns and hybrid attacks from Russia.

While there are still some changes necessary, of course, we cannot allow Moscow to undermine Moldova's European cause.

Russia's actions remind us that enlargement is not a bureaucratic exercise, but one of the EU's most important geopolitical instruments to strengthen stability, security and prosperity across our continent.

Candidate countries must deliver on reforms. At the same time, the EU has to remain a reliable partner.

discussion.speaker: Maria GRAPINI
discussion.text:
Doamnă comisar, domnule președinte, stimați colegi, programul ambițios al Republicii Moldova pentru a încheia aderarea la sfârșitul anului 2028 trebuie susținut. Este de salutat, dar nu va putea fi pus în aplicare dacă nu îl susținem toți. Și vreau de la bun început să mulțumesc și doamnei comisar, și colegilor care au susținut acest proiect.

Sunt româncă, sunt moldoveancă, cunosc foarte bine Republica Moldova, cunosc cetățenii de acolo, cetățenii își doresc acest lucru și trebuie să-i încurajăm pentru a avea încredere în proiectul Uniunii Europene, pentru că are nevoie administrația de la Chișinău de susținerea populară.

Sigur că nu văd alt drum și trebuie să fim și realiști: Republica Moldova e la graniță, cât de greu este să reziste la atacurile directe, indirecte, fake news-urile și tot ce se întâmplă acolo cu Rusia. Uniunea Europeană este un proiect la care eu, ca româncă, mi-am dorit să fim cu țara mea acolo. De aceea, doamna comisar, Consiliul, Parlamentul trebuie să înțeleagă că Republica Moldova are locul ei în Uniunea Europeană și trebuie să o susținem.

Și mai vreau să adaug un lucru: cred foarte tare că ceea ce acum se întâmplă în Ucraina ține în loc și Republica Moldova. Trebuie să separăm. România și Bulgaria a pățit același lucru cu Schengen. Haideți să fim corecți, obiectivi - în Ucraina nu se pot respecta termenele și jaloanele - și să dăm drumul Moldovei și, la terminarea anului 2028, Republica Moldova să fie în marea familie.

translation.englishText:
Madam Commissioner, Mr President, dear colleagues, the ambitious program of the Republic of Moldova to conclude accession by the end of 2028 must be supported. It is to be welcomed, but it will not be able to be implemented if we do not all support it. And I want from the very beginning to thank both the Commissioner and the colleagues who have supported this project.

I am Romanian, I am Moldovan, I know the Republic of Moldova very well, I know the citizens there, the citizens want this and we must encourage them to have confidence in the European Union project, because the administration in Chisinau needs popular support.

Of course, I see no other path and we must also be realistic: the Republic of Moldova is at the border, how difficult it is to resist direct and indirect attacks, fake news and everything that happens there with Russia. The European Union is a project that I, as a Romanian, wanted us to be there with my country. Therefore, Madam Commissioner, the Council, the Parliament must understand that the Republic of Moldova has its place in the European Union and we must support it.

And I also want to add one thing: I strongly believe that what is happening now in Ukraine is also holding back the Republic of Moldova. We must separate them. Romania and Bulgaria experienced the same thing with Schengen. Let us be fair, objective - in Ukraine the deadlines and milestones cannot be respected - and let us give Moldova the green light and, at the end of 2028, the Republic of Moldova should be in the great family.

discussion.speaker: Şerban Dimitrie STURDZA
discussion.text:
Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, mă bucur că Republica Moldova a deschis primul capitol de negociere pentru aderarea la Uniunea Europeană. De acum, datoria noastră este să nu transformăm acest drum european într-o sală de așteptare fără sfârșit. Republica Moldova trebuie evaluată corect. Este firesc ca România să susțină Republica Moldova în parcursul său de aderare la Uniunea Europeană.

Sprijinirea românilor de peste Prut este o datorie istorică și o necesitate strategică. Cu atât mai mult cu cât aproape jumătate din ei sunt și cetățeni ai României. Integrarea sa în Uniunea Europeană reprezintă mai multă stabilitate și mai multă siguranță la frontiera estică a Uniunii. Însă Republica Moldova trebuie să continue să se desprindă de moștenirea sa sovietică, precum și de reflexele trecutului, iar Bruxelles-ul trebuie să-și dovedească deschiderea pentru un rezultat final concret și neîntârziat.

Dacă românii de peste ambele maluri ale Prutului nu s-au putut reunifica precum berlinezii, atunci Republica Moldova și România trebuie să se reunifice măcar prin apartenența lor la Uniunea Europeană.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, I am glad that the Republic of Moldova has opened the first negotiation chapter for accession to the European Union. From now on, our duty is not to turn this European path into an endless waiting room. The Republic of Moldova must be correctly evaluated. It is natural for Romania to support the Republic of Moldova in its EU accession path.

Supporting the Romanians across the Prut is a historical duty and a strategic necessity. All the more so since almost half of them are also citizens of Romania. Its integration into the European Union represents more stability and more security at the eastern border of the Union. However, the Republic of Moldova must continue to break away from its Soviet heritage and the reflexes of the past, and Brussels must prove its openness for a concrete and prompt final result.

If the Romanians from both banks of the Prut could not reunite like the Berliners, then the Republic of Moldova and Romania must reunite at least through their belonging to the European Union.
translation.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, mă bucur că Republica Moldova a deschis primul capitol de negociere pentru aderarea la Uniunea Europeană. De acum, datoria noastră este să nu transformăm acest drum european într-o sală de așteptare fără sfârșit. Republica Moldova trebuie evaluată corect. Este firesc ca România să susțină Republica Moldova în parcursul său de aderare la Uniunea Europeană.

Sprijinirea românilor de peste Prut este o datorie istorică și o necesitate strategică. Cu atât mai mult cu cât aproape jumătate din ei sunt și cetățeni ai României. Integrarea sa în Uniunea Europeană reprezintă mai multă stabilitate și mai multă siguranță la frontiera estică a Uniunii. discussion.speaker: Krzysztof BREJZA
discussion.text:
Panie Przewodniczący! Mołdawia daje nadzieję tak potrzebną dziś Unii Europejskiej, bo członkostwo Mołdawii w Unii Europejskiej pokazuje, że te starania europejskie to coś więcej niż zabieganie o fundusze, o instytucje. To walka o wartości. I ta droga europejska Mołdawii pokazuje, że można pokonać ruski mir, że można wygrać z ruskimi służbami. Z tym Goliatem Dawid może wygrać prawdą, konsekwencją i determinacją.

Mołdawia jest dla nas wzorcem, w jaki sposób walczyć z oligarchami, którzy próbują destabilizować nasze społeczeństwa, jak walczyć z kłamstwem, ale też jak walczyć z takimi zjawiskami jak kryptowaluty, które nadal w niektórych państwach Unii Europejskiej używane są do niszczenia demokracji, niszczenia Unii Europejskiej. Bierzmy przykład z Mołdawii – małego, ale wielkiego duchem państwa.

translation.englishText:
Mr President! Moldova gives the hope so much needed today by the European Union, because Moldova's membership in the European Union shows that these European efforts are something more than campaigning for funds, for institutions. It is a fight for values. And this European path of Moldova shows that the Russkiy Mir can be overcome, that you can win against Russian services. Against this Goliath, David can win with truth, consistency and determination.

Moldova is a model for us in how to fight oligarchs who try to destabilize our societies, how to fight lies, but also how to fight phenomena such as cryptocurrencies, which in some European Union member states are still used to destroy democracy, to destroy the European Union. Let us take an example from Moldova – a small country, but great in spirit.

Mołdawia daje nadzieję tak potrzebną dziś Unii Europejskiej, bo członkostwo Mołdawii w Unii Europejskiej pokazuje, że te starania europejskie to coś więcej niż zabieganie o fundusze, o instytucje. Bierzmy przykład z Mołdawii – małego, ale wielkiego duchem państwa.

discussion.speaker: Vytenis Povilas ANDRIUKAITIS
discussion.text:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, thank you for the excellent report, Sven Mikser. I cannot stress enough the importance of opening all negotiation clusters for Moldova and Ukraine. Article 49 of the Treaty of European Union clearly states that unanimity is required only for the opening and closing of accession negotiations. But what is the European Council doing? The endless unanimity silos for each chapter are like sand that the Council is throwing in the gears of enlargement.

The situation now is that the Member States are undermining European security, delaying the enlargement process, sabotaging our strategic interests and preventing effective, comprehensive negotiations on all clusters with Moldova. Let us do our best to fulfil our promise to start closing all chapters at the beginning of 2027, as promised.

Dear friends in Moldova and Ukraine, please continue your reforms with the same spirit as before. Please trust us, and we will do our utmost to have you sitting in this Parliament among us in the nearest future. Let's do it!

discussion.speaker: Liudas MAŽYLIS
discussion.text: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Moldova šiandien demonstruoja įspūdingą europinį pagreitį: užbaigta dvišalė patikra, visi šeši narystės derybų klasteriai jau potencialiai atverti, o dvidešimt keturi iš dvidešimt šešių reformos žingsnių jau įgyvendinti. Matoma akivaizdi pažanga pamatinių vertybių, vidaus rinkos ir išorės santykių srityse. Moldova toliau bando nuosekliai judėti išteklių, žemės ūkio bei sanglaudos kryptimis. Mums, Europos Sąjungai, tai argumentas veikti drąsiai ir atverti derybas dėl narystės, parodant, kad reformos duoda realų politinį rezultatą. Žinoma, Rusijos karinis buvimas Padniestrėje yra tarptautinės teisės pažeidimas ir tiesioginė grėsmė. Rusai privalo besąlygiškai pasitraukti, o mes privalome padėti Moldovai stiprinti atsparumą energetinę nepriklausomybę ir pasitikėjimą europiniu keliu.

translation.englishText: Mr. President, Commissioner, colleagues. Today, Moldova is demonstrating impressive European momentum: bilateral screening is complete, all six accession negotiation clusters are potentially open, and twenty-four out of twenty-six reform steps have already been implemented. Clear progress is visible in the areas of fundamental values, the internal market, and external relations. Moldova continues to try to move consistently in the directions of resources, agriculture, and cohesion. For us, the European Union, this is an argument to act boldly and open membership negotiations, showing that reforms yield real political results. Of course, Russia's military presence in Transnistria is a violation of international law and a direct threat. The Russians must withdraw unconditionally, and we must help Moldova strengthen its resilience, energy independence, and confidence in the European path.

discussion.speaker: Gheorghe FALCĂ
discussion.text:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, doamnelor și domnilor, astăzi nu decidem doar asupra parcursului european al Republicii Moldova. Decidem și cât de credibilă este Uniunea Europeană atunci când un popor își asumă valorile noastre și are curajul să le apere.

Republica Moldova nu cere favoruri. Vine cu reforme, cu sacrificii și cu alegere democratică reafirmate de cetățenii săi. Vine cu demnitate și cu rezistența remarcabilă în fața presiunii și amenințării ruse. De aceea, Republica Moldova nu este doar un stat candidat. Este dovada că proiectul european inspiră, mobilizează și oferă speranțe. Pentru România acest sprijin este o responsabilitate istorică. Pentru Uniunea Europeană, este o chestiune de credibilitate.

Nu putem cere curaj celor care aleg Europa și apoi să-i părăsim. Reformele trebuie să continue în Moldova, iar noi trebuie să răspundem cu un sprijin ferm și consecvent. Astăzi, votul nostru trebuie să fie direct pentru Moldova, cât și pentru Uniunea Europeană unită.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, today we are not only deciding on the European path of the Republic of Moldova. We are also deciding how credible the European Union is when a people embraces our values and has the courage to defend them.

The Republic of Moldova is not asking for favors. It comes with reforms, sacrifices, and a democratic choice reaffirmed by its citizens. It comes with dignity and remarkable resilience in the face of Russian pressure and threats. That is why the Republic of Moldova is not just a candidate state. It is proof that the European project inspires, mobilizes, and offers hope. For Romania, this support is a historical responsibility. For the European Union, it is a matter of credibility.

We cannot ask for courage from those who choose Europe and then abandon them. Reforms must continue in Moldova, and we must respond with firm and consistent support. Today, our vote must be directly for Moldova, as well as for a united European Union.
translation.sourceText:

Nu putem cere curaj celor care aleg Europa și apoi să-i părăsim. Reformele trebuie să continue în Moldova, iar noi trebuie să răspundem cu un sprijin ferm și consecvent. Astăzi, votul nostru trebuie să fie direct pentru Moldova, cât și pentru Uniunea Europeană unită.

discussion.speaker: Oliver SCHENK
discussion.text:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Moldau steht erneut an einem Wendepunkt. Die jüngsten politischen Entwicklungen in Chișinău zeigen, wie sensibel die innenpolitische Lage bleibt und wie entscheidend Stabilität, Reformfähigkeit und ein klarer europäischer Kurs jetzt sind.

Gerade vor diesem Hintergrund halte ich diesen Bericht für besonders wichtig. Er zeigt deutlich: Moldau hat trotz enormen äußeren Drucks bemerkenswerte Fortschritte gemacht im EU‑Beitrittsprozess – bei Reformen im Justiz- und Verwaltungsbereich und bei der wirtschaftlichen Annäherung an die Europäische Union.

Aber wir dürfen nicht naiv sein. Moldau steht unter einem anhaltenden hybriden Angriff – Desinformation, Cyberangriffe, Energie-Erpressung und russische Einflussnahme zielen darauf, den europäischen Kurs des Landes zu brechen.

Unsere Antwort muss klar sein: Wir unterstützen Moldau politisch, finanziell und sicherheitspolitisch. Die Beitrittsverhandlungen müssen auf Leistung beruhen, nicht auf Blockaden. Wer Reformen liefert, muss Fortschritt sehen. Moldaus europäische Zukunft ist nicht nur eine moldauische Frage, sie ist eine Frage der Glaubwürdigkeit und Sicherheit Europas.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues! Moldova is once again at a turning point. The recent political developments in Chișinău show how sensitive the domestic political situation remains and how crucial stability, the capacity for reform, and a clear European course are now.

Against this very background, I consider this report to be particularly important. It clearly shows that Moldova has made remarkable progress in the EU accession process despite enormous external pressure – in judicial and administrative reforms and in economic rapprochement with the European Union.

But we must not be naive. Moldova is under sustained hybrid attack – disinformation, cyber attacks, energy blackmail, and Russian influence aim to break the country's European course.

Our response must be clear: We support Moldova politically, financially, and in terms of security policy. Accession negotiations must be based on performance, not blockades. Those who deliver reforms must see progress. Moldova's European future is not just a Moldovan issue, it is a question of Europe's credibility and security.

discussion.speaker: Michał SZCZERBA
discussion.text:
Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Mołdawia jest wyjątkowym krajem kandydatem. I chciałbym bardzo serdecznie podziękować również Pani, Pani Komisarz, że od samego początku stawia Pani na Mołdawię – na kraj, który również według tego przedstawionego sprawozdania ma największe postępy, jeśli chodzi o przygotowania do członkostwa. I chcemy to bardzo wyraźnie powiedzieć.

Ale to jest też kraj, który inspiruje i który motywuje również odpowiedzialnością za odporność społeczną i demokratyczną, za rozumienie, czym jest bezpieczeństwo, czym są zagrożenia hybrydowe obecne wokół naszego sąsiedztwa.

Jako sprawozdawca ds. mobilności wojskowej zaproponowałem, żeby Mołdawia była jednym z bliskich partnerów, którzy zostaną uwzględnieni w tej regulacji, ponieważ budując mobilność wojskową, budując korytarze mobilności, chcemy uwzględnić również kraje kandydujące. Mołdawia ma tam swoje miejsce.

translation.englishText:
Mr President! Madam Commissioner! Moldova is a unique candidate country. And I would like to very warmly thank you as well, Madam Commissioner, that from the very beginning you have been betting on Moldova - on a country which, also according to this presented report, has the greatest progress when it comes to preparations for membership. And we want to state this very clearly.

But this is also a country that inspires and motivates also through responsibility for social and democratic resilience, for understanding what security is, what hybrid threats are present around our neighbourhood.

As the rapporteur for military mobility, I proposed that Moldova be one of the close partners to be included in this regulation, because by building military mobility, by building mobility corridors, we also want to include candidate countries. Moldova has its place there.

discussion.speaker: Nikola MINCHEV
discussion.text:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the 2025 report on Moldova sends a clear message: despite an extremely challenging geopolitical and economic environment, Moldova continues to move forward on its European path.

The progress is concrete. Moldova is replacing its Soviet-era standards with European ones. These are not merely technical changes, but tangible steps, improving quality, safety and protection for Moldovan citizens. We also see progress in consumer protection. Moldova has made public services more accessible and effective.

Notably, Moldova has consistently cooperated on foreign policy issues, and aligns with the EU's common foreign and security policy positions. This is done in a very hostile environment, under significant internal and external challenges, such as persistent hostile Russian interference, as correctly noted in the report.

Of course, challenges remain and further work is needed, but today we should recognise the progress achieved. Moldova is making serious efforts, delivering concrete results and demonstrating through action its European ambitions.

These efforts deserve our recognition and our continued support, because we do not see them everywhere, and we value them when we see them.

discussion.speaker: Alvise PÉREZ
discussion.text:
Señor presidente, no entiendo en absoluto qué hacéis algunos diputados —casi todos españoles— aplaudiendo la ampliación de la Unión Europea antes en el debate anterior de Ucrania y ahora en el de Moldavia.

Que lo hagan los alemanes lo puedo entender, pero nosotros, los españoles, ¿no hemos leído aquí el estudio interno filtrado del propio Consejo de la Unión Europea en 2023, en el que se señala que España va a ser el único país que va a pasar de cobrar a pagar? ¿Saben ustedes lo que significan 3 000 millones de euros de la PAC menos para un agricultor en España, en Rumanía, en Portugal o en Italia?

¿Saben lo que significa meter al país más pobre de Europa, que es Moldavia, con 2,4 millones de habitantes —lo sé porque he estado en Moldavia como voluntario, con refugiados de Moldavia— y con una corrupción sistémica del 12 % del PIB? Hablamos de meter ahora mismo a un territorio que tiene 1 500 soldados rusos dentro, en Transnistria, con un referéndum europeo, por cierto, que sacó un 50,4 %, y gracias al voto de la diáspora, porque uno de cada tres moldavos viven fuera de su país.

En fin, entiendo que algunos sí, pero que los diputados españoles apoyen esto me parece surrealista.

translation.englishText:
Mr President, I completely do not understand what some MEPs—almost all of them Spanish—are doing, applauding the enlargement of the European Union, earlier in the previous debate on Ukraine and now in this one on Moldova.

That the Germans do it, I can understand, but we Spaniards, have we not read here the leaked internal study from the Council of the European Union itself in 2023, which indicates that Spain is going to be the only country that will go from being a net recipient to a net contributor? Do you know what 3 billion euros less from the CAP means for a farmer in Spain, in Romania, in Portugal, or in Italy?

Do you know what it means to bring in the poorest country in Europe, which is Moldova, with 2.4 million inhabitants—I know this because I have been to Moldova as a volunteer, with refugees from Moldova—and with systemic corruption amounting to 12% of GDP? We are talking about bringing in right now a territory that has 1,500 Russian soldiers inside it, in Transnistria, with a European referendum, by the way, that yielded 50.4%, and thanks to the diaspora vote, because one in three Moldovans lives outside their country.

Anyway, I understand that some do, but for Spanish MEPs to support this seems surreal to me.

discussion.speaker: Marta Kos
discussion.text:
Mr President, honourable members of the European Parliament, it's really good to see that Moldova has so many supporters here in the European Parliament. Some of them are very passionate. Mr Andriukaitis, thank you for your passionate words. I am on your side. I would also like to see Members of the European Parliament from Moldova as soon as possible too.

Moldova has demonstrated determination and delivered meaningful reforms under exceptionally challenging circumstances. It deserves recognition for that progress and our continued support to move forward on its path to EU membership. We have organised the biggest investment conference to date at the beginning of June in Chişinău and the companies from the Member States are already coming. This is the only way to prosperity. So, they have to do the reforms, the investors will come, and then we can speak about the prosperity.

Regarding the question of when Moldova will be able to become a member of the EU: when all the reforms will be done, meaning Moldova has to deliver, but we have to deliver too. I have heard this today many times. So, it is also our responsibility that this will happen as soon as possible. I used to say that Moldova is the best student in my class. Since the last successful way on the reforms, I am saying that Moldova is the best performer in my class.

discussion.speaker: Sven MIKSER
discussion.text:
Mr President, first of all, I would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs. It was really intellectually stimulating and a very constructive effort that produced this report. I think that all the pro-European groups who negotiated the report were brought together by a great sense of unity of purpose, but also a sense of urgency. I would also like to thank Commissioner Kos for her personal dedication and commitment to supporting, in every possible way, Moldova's very legitimate European aspirations. And I would like to thank all the colleagues for an extremely constructive debate here.

I hope that the report that we are going to be voting on tomorrow – and also tonight's debate – help us to send a very clear message to the Moldovan people and the Moldovan Government: a message of support and solidarity, but also a message of what our expectations are as to the next steps to be taken in this reform path.

I also hope that the report and the debates send a very clear message to our colleagues, the political leaders in our Member State capitals, who periodically meet around the Council table: a message that we expect them to live up to our end of the bargain, as I said, and to actually act with the same sense of urgency, because it is absolutely clear that the Russian pressure on Moldova will not dissipate until the successful completion of this process.

Moldova did not apply for membership and we did not launch this process in order for us to allow them to enjoy the process. It must be a purpose-driven process that will conclude in fully integrating Moldova into our European family without any unnecessary delay.

discussion.speaker: Martin HOJSÍK (Chair)
discussion.text:
Ďakujem spravodajcovi a všetkým zúčastneným v debate, ako aj pani komisárke.

Rozprava k tomuto bodu sa týmto skončila a hlasovanie sa uskutoční zajtra.

translation.englishText:
Thank you to the rapporteur and everyone who participated in the debate, as well as to the Commissioner.

The debate on this item is now concluded and the vote will take place tomorrow.
translation.sourceText:
Ďakujem spravodajcovi a všetkým zúčastneným v debate, ako aj pani komisárke.

Rozprava k tomuto bodu sa týmto skončila a hlasovanie sa uskutoční zajtra.

speaker: Luis-Vicențiu Lazarus
text:
Domnule președinte, dragi colegi, eu nu am să mă înscriu în corul lăudătorilor acestei chestiuni cu aderarea Moldovei și Ucrainei la Uniunea Europeană, pentru că eu știam că întotdeauna aceste țări care sunt candidate trebuie să respecte niște criterii. Și criteriul corupției, care este printre primele, nu este deloc respectat. Așa cum știți, probabil Moldova nu mai are premier. Tocmai și-a dat demisia.

De ce și-a dat demisia? În ce context și-a dat demisia? În contextul în care verișoara Maiei Sandu, pseudo președinta acestei pseudo republici... pentru că, de fapt, nu e a noastră Moldova? E parte din România. Mă frapează faptul că nimeni nu spune treaba asta aici, ca și cum ar fi fost normal un pact Ribbentrop-Molotov, de pildă.

Deci ne-am trezit cu verișoara președintei că are salariu de 6000, peste 6000 de euro. Păi noi ajutăm Moldova, noi ducem acolo miliarde pentru reforme și ei își dau salarii de 6000. Dar nu vi se pare (...)

(Președintele a retras cuvântul vorbitorului)

translation.englishText:
Mr. President, dear colleagues, I will not join the choir of glorifiers of this matter regarding the accession of Moldova and Ukraine to the European Union, because I knew that always these candidate countries must meet certain criteria. And the corruption criterion, which is among the first, is not respected at all. As you probably know, Moldova no longer has a prime minister. They just resigned.

Why did they resign? In what context did they resign? In the context where Maia Sandu's cousin, the pseudo-president of this pseudo-republic... because, in fact, isn't Moldova ours? It is part of Romania. It strikes me that no one says this thing here, as if a Ribbentrop-Molotov pact, for example, had been normal.

So we woke up finding out that the president's cousin has a salary of 6000, over 6000 euros. Well, we are helping Moldova, we are bringing billions there for reforms and they are giving themselves salaries of 6000. But doesn't it seem to you (...)

(The President withdrew the speaker's floor)
